summary: After a close race, voters who backed the winner are glad and voters who did not say they will wait and see.
realLife: A Rochester, Minnesota mayor was elected by just under 700 votes, 1.2 percent. A New York City mayor was elected with nearly half the city's voters not supporting the winner, and the paper asked what those voters do now.
sources: KTTC, Rochester mayoral candidates share reactions to election results: https://www.kttc.com/2026/11/04/rochester-mayoral-candidates-share-reactions-election-results/?outputType=amp
Yahoo News, Nearly half of NYC voters opposed the winner. What do they do now?: https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/nearly-half-nyc-voted-against-080017431.html
inGame: lean-with and lean-against in the bring-it-up rows: the speaker says whether their own ballot went to {winner}.

turns.turn: The ballot went to the winner
turns.pull: the speaker's recorded vote or lean was for the winner
turns.writes: writes glad, and says so in a line

turns.pull: the speaker's vote or lean was for another
turns.writes: writes wait and see, or not happy, and says so in a line
